name: TraceLab
description: AI-powered Rust codebase scanner and visual payload flow simulator

1_scanner.title: Codebase Scanner
1_scanner.description: Scans any local Rust workspace, detects services from Cargo.toml files, reads all .rs files, sends them to an LLM for semantic analysis, and produces a structured JSON graph.
details: Walks workspace directory tree looking for Cargo.toml files
Identifies workspace root vs member crates automatically
Reads all .rs files per service (up to 100KB each), preserving service context
Sends batched source per service to LLM with structured JSON schema prompt
Parallel analysis — up to 5 services concurrently
Cross-service relationship analysis pass (shared structs, HTTP calls, message queues)
Merges all results into a single <service-name>.tracelab.json file written to the scanned workspace root
Checks for existing .tracelab.json before re-scanning (skips LLM if cached, rescan via checkbox)
Streams progress events to the UI in real-time via NDJSON

output_schema.nodes: id, service, kind (route_handler | transformer | validator | middleware | business_logic | db_call | external_http_call | struct | enum | message_queue | function), name, input, output, mutates_state, mutation_target, defined_in, description, method, path_pattern, handler, fields, used_by_services, source_code, example_payload, port
output_schema.mutations: id, service, kind, mutates, via, in_component, defined_in
output_schema.cross_service_calls: id, kind, from_service, to_service, via, endpoint, payload_in, payload_out, defined_in

2_visualizer.title: React Flow Visual Graph
2_visualizer.description: Loads the .tracelab.json and renders an interactive layered graph with services as container boxes and components as nodes inside them.
details: Services rendered as colored container boxes with header (name, description, icon)
Components stacked vertically inside services, topologically sorted by edge order
6 color themes cycling across services (blue, emerald, purple, amber, rose, cyan)
11 component kinds with distinct colors and type badges (ROUTE, MIDDLEWARE, HANDLER, DB, TRANSFORM, VALIDATOR, EXTERNAL, STRUCT, ENUM, QUEUE, FN)
Intra-service edges: subtle gray smooth-step paths
Cross-service edges: dashed green bezier curves
Animated dot follows edge path during simulation
Pan, zoom, fit-to-view controls
Dot grid background
Filter: only flow-relevant nodes shown on canvas (structs/enums hidden unless they participate in edges)
Load via file path input, query parameter (?path=), or JSON file upload
2_visualizer.layout_algorithm: Dagre at service level (LR) for inter-service positioning; manual vertical stacking within each service; topological sort for component order

3_simulator.title: LLM-Powered Payload Simulation
3_simulator.description: Simulates payload flow through the component graph without running the actual Rust server. Each component is simulated by the LLM based on its kind, description, and source code.
details: Select any entry point (route handler or any component) to start simulation
Provide initial JSON payload in the UI
BFS traversal from start node through edges to determine execution order
Each node simulated by LLM: receives input payload, returns output payload + explanation + diff summary
Output payload of one node becomes input payload of the next
Streaming simulation events to UI in real-time via NDJSON
Visual feedback: active node highlighted (blue glow), completed nodes (green ring), pending nodes dimmed
Edge animation: dot travels along edge path when data flows between nodes
Right sidebar panel with 3 tabs: Inspector (controls + component details), Payload (input/output JSON), Log (event trace)
Component-specific simulation prompts: route_handler validates/parses, transformer modifies shape, validator accepts/rejects, db_call returns query result, middleware adds/checks headers

4_breakpoints.title: Interactive Breakpoint Debugger
4_breakpoints.description: Pause simulation at any component boundary, inspect the payload, edit it, and resume to see how downstream components process the modified data.
details: Click the circle on any component node to toggle a breakpoint (amber fill when set, left border highlight)
When simulation reaches a breakpoint, it pauses and opens the Breakpoint Editor modal
Modal shows: incoming payload (read-only) and editable JSON textarea
Real-time JSON validation in the editor
Resume with edits: modified payload continues through the rest of the graph
Resume as-is: original payload continues unchanged
Breakpoints persist across simulation runs (cleared on explicit reset)
Visual indicators: amber left border on breakpointed nodes, amber status in Inspector panel

POST /api/scan.description: Scans a Rust workspace and produces a .tracelab.json graph

POST /api/load-graph.description: Loads a .tracelab.json or components.json from disk

POST /api/simulate.description: Runs LLM-powered simulation through the component graph
POST /api/simulate.response: NDJSON stream of SimulationEvent (step | breakpoint | complete | error)

pages./: Scanner — enter workspace path, select LLM provider, scan
pages./visualize: Visualizer — load .tracelab.json, interactive graph, simulation, breakpoints

future_phases.phase_3: Runtime instrumentation — attach to running Rust services via tracing/proc-macro, stream live payload events over WebSocket, overlay on static graph
future_phases.phase_4: Payload debugger — pause in-flight payloads at component boundaries in a live running system, inspect/edit/replay
